welcome to another video my friends this is the story and artwork Martin Ramirez was born on the 30th of January 1895 into pedan within the Jalisco most of Ramirez's early life remains shrouded in some mystery on May 31st 1918 he married 17-year-old Maria Santa Ana Navaro Basquez after relocating to TT the couple gave birth to their three daughters Joanna tioa and Austina and Ramirez bought a small piece of land on credit in a ranch near San Gracia by 1925 however Ramirez set his sight to the neighboring land of opportunity in the United States leaving his three daughters and his wife pregnant with his soon Tobe born only son to work on the California railroads to earn more money to support his family this decision would lead to many unfortunate circumstances later down the line as conflict in his home country was reaching breaking points in the wake of the cero war that ultimately would family by the start of the 1930s Ramirez found himself cut off from both his family and the entire world around him eventually ending up unemployed and homeless within a country of which he could hardly speak the language spiraling into a terrible battle with his mental health whilst living on the 1931 Ramirez was picked up by the San Wen County California police and committed to Stockton State Hospital where he received a preliminary depression after escaping the hospital twice within the 2 years that followed he was committed to the hospital again after a few days in jail and diagnosed with a catatonic form of dementia precox he would even Escape Stockton a third time by 1934 but returned of his own valtion after spending three or 4 streets however it would be during these artistic talent began to emerge using whatever materials he could find including scraps of paper scavenged pencils crayons cardboard and even potato paste mixed with his saliva he began recreating his memories within collages a turning point came in 1948 when Ramirez was transferred to the dit Sacramento it was here where a visiting recognized the Brilliance in Ramirez's work Pasto began collecting and preserving Ramirez's Creations many of which were sprawling narratives filled references over the course of his life Ramirez produced some 500 Works characteristic for their clean yet draftsmanship the imagery is both reminiscent of his own life experiences Mexican madonas animals Cowboys trains Landscapes merge with the scenes of American culture and create a profound documentation of a Mexican living and States despite pasto's efforts Ramirez remained largely unknown during his lifetime exhibiting his work in small exhibitions as early as the 1950s it wasn't until the 70s long after 1963 that his work gained wider attention artists Jim nut and Gladis Nelson along with the art dealer Phyllis kind championed Ramirez's art organizing larger exhibitions and acquiring a collection since then Ramirez's work has been celebrated for its raw honesty imagery he is considered to be a master of self-taught artists of the 20th century his legacy a testament to the power of human creativity that can flourish even in the most challenging circumstances with a mind so the first work I'd like us to explore is 1954 unofficial because from what I understand most if not all of his pieces were all left Untitled and this will be the case for all of the work we'll be taking a look at in this video in the midst of all of these the first thing that tends to grab the eye is a central figure with an Indescribable expression on their face emerging from some kind of portal in a arches this placement suggests a place of sanctuary a refuge within the artwork itself the religious iconography could hold personal significance for Ramirez perhaps it reflects a source of Solace stability within the conf findes of the Asylum a place where Familiar Comfort flanking the central figure are intriguing animal forms these creatures might represent a connection to the Natural World a stark contrast of a Asylum the presence could symbolize a yearning for Freedom a desire to escape the openness and simplicity of nature looming large in the upper portion of the artwork is a train and its tracks trains were a recurring Motif in Ramirez's work likely a powerful memory from his past working on the California railroad here the train might symbolize a bygone era a time of freedom and movement that stands in stark contrast interpreted as a representation of the structured routine and repetitive nature of life within the Asylum as we will come to see in other examples of his work this entire scene is brimming with intricate and repetitive patterns and a Relentless use of horizontal and parallel lines while some may interpret this repetition as a symptom of his schizophrenia it could also be seen as a form of artistic compulsion and a method of creating order within his world these patterns might also function as a form of personal expression a visual experiences while some of his Works seem to have explored the inner world of Ramirez others would symbolize his memories experiences and upbringing such as this next work that bears The Unofficial title of cabalero with women 1953 we're greeted Again by a frame of repetitive lines that create The Surreal stage for our Central figures here this introduces us to another element of Ramirez's use of collage in particular the woman on the left armed with a gun I managed to come across an exhibition pamphlet online courtesy of a folkart museum in New York which uncovers a great deal of information on his individual pieces including this one especially in regards to what these figures symbolize I've also left a link for this in the description below if you want to take a look for yourself according to the pamphlet the significance of the rider on the horse proudly holding his pistol is best explained by Martin Ramirez's oldest daughter xanna who explains her father used to say that having a good horse and a good pistol would make a man happy as these were considered to be two very important symbols of masculinity and social status among the rural poor of the Rancho Society where he lived until he was 30 years old it was also reported that Ramirez was an excellent Rider of his bay horse the small drawings that Ramirez sent back to his family with his letters before he was interned in the first mental hospital were mainly of Riders though the layers behind this symbolism don't stop there Ramirez's biography suggests that his Riders had an intimate connection to the chero Rebellion that took place between 1926 1929 this conflict between armed Catholic Rebels and the secular government of Mexico had devastating effects on Ramirez's family and on the lives of other rural impoverished families from Los Altos D Jalisco which was the central area of a Revolt the federal army forced fields to be abandoned and thousands of families including Ramirez's own to leave behind all their belongings and concentrate in towns but the reality of this conflict escalated Beyond eviction of locals the Army also took possession of all remaining crops in the countryside set pastures and Fields on fire and turned their machine guns on any cattle or animals that they could not take away by train all religious acts and processions were suspended the churches were closed later plundered and used as Stables troops this situation must have seemed nothing short of apocalyptic for Ramirez he once even received a letter from his brother explaining how he had only been able to escape execution thanks to Ramirez's wife and a friend his brother wrote about the destruction of Ramirez his property and the loss of all his animals after a long wait Ramirez sent a letter back to his brother telling him he was not coming home to Jalisco this letter made it clear to his family that Ramirez had completely misunderstood his brother's letter and mistakenly believed that his wife in absence had abandoned her duties as mother and wife and left her family to ride off on Horseback to fight with the federal army against the cheros next I'd like us to take a closer look at Martin Ramirez's use of collage specifically within his Untitled piece completed in 1952 showing again how Ramirez would often create Arts with whatever materials he had available within such a restrictive environment surrounded by the thick walls of a mental hospital the situation for many patients must have been prison-like exchanges with the outside were drastically reduced and made exclusively through third parties such as Ward magazines just like a DJ or a music producer uses other tracks as quaries to give form to new ideas collage Arts functions in a very Sim similar way whether you call it collage cut and paste or sampling the practice of remains a fascinating process which Ramirez does very beautifully here as the folk art museum explains quote the the varial engineer leaning out of a window of his powerful and impressive locomotive it is a concentrated image of desire and a possibly Amorous encounter at the same time we Face a representation via an erotic setting of The mythologized Clash of the Wild and the authentic West represented here by the woman with the strength of the modern machine age represented here by the train Ramirez picked up this cliche in transferring it into his collage transformed its meaning into the opposite there is an obvious contrast between his stylish illustration of the woman on the one hand and Ramirez's simple and delightful completion of a horse and the rough hatching on the borders this contrast becomes even more acute when one recalls the conditions under which the collage was produced Ramirez had cut off all contact with his family in Mexico and remains in California he ended up confined to a mental Asylum knowing that never again would he be on a train back home thus this cheerful image of a glamorous en counter turns into a metaphor for quote this next piece unofficially titled Madonna is an intriguing addition to his body of work this in fact would just be one example of many Works depicting the image of the Madonna which is linked to a very Dee rooted cultural signific ific an the representation of a Madonna is very common in Mexican religious art and popular expression whether for institutional domestic or personal use virgins depicted in many forms abound in paintings sculptures ex votos prints medals and even tattoos on the skin Roman Catholicism in Mexico is a fusion of indigenous and European belief systems and traditions depending on ethnicity cultural region social class and Rural or Urban context Mexican dynamically as we know Ramirez created art in a very restrictive environment with barely any adequate materials it is said he often worked on the floor of his Hospital Ward choosing a studio Space barded by two twin beds and a nightstand the artists collected a variety of papers such as discarded newspapers book pages flattened paper cups and examining table cover sheets Glu them together with homemade adfs his glue recipe included potato starch bread dough and saliva it was only later after his work began to Garner notice that art supplies were given to him by Dr Pasto and Hospital staff Ramirez then collected crayons color pencils water-based paints and Poss also shoe polish and fruit juices then crushed these materials into a liquid medium that he mixed into a pot rather than use a brush he used a match stick as his form of stylus and for a straight edge he used a tongue depressor when it came to his larger scale work such as the Madonna piece we're looking at now he would stand on a table to evaluate his artwork laid out on the floor from an appropriate distance across the work we can see Blobs of swirling lines that almost Contours the lines have nearly perfect spacing indicating a sense of order that Ramirez forcibly brings to the scene as well as a Clarity and sense of control over the direction of his artistic expression while it might seem unlikely Ramirez did have an audience artist Wayne tabal remembers visiting him with art classes from a nearby College and would recount his experience quote I met him and watched him work he used little prototypes he would roll up and put in his jacket to copy like a foot or a head or a train or a Horse and Rider it seems he had a kind of series of little characters that he would bring on stage almost like a repitor company he pasted papers together with a mixture of breads from the mes hle and his saliva and would past together all kinds of bits of material of all sorts of paper he could quote in this other example of a Madonna completed between 1950 and 1953 Ramirez executes this piece in a similarly rustic setting except this time we're given subtle imagery of a setting which resembles a chapel within a church or Shrine in a workplace or home this style may be related to prints or tar Jettas common templates for artists with no dressed in a robe with Hues of celestial blue the Virgin stands on a tripod that resembles a traditional mil jet around volcanic rock artifact and common tool used since pre-colombian times to grind sources it form asserts the shape of the architectural setting are branches of Lies the flowers are always accompanied the Virgin symbolizing Purity and feathers also hold a symbolic purpose worth mentioning here feathers were sacred material used only by the highest abbility by Warriors and in the ritual deities feathers were so valuable that they were also used as materials to pay tribute in early colonial Mexican art indigenous artists use feathers to make Mosaic paintings as gift for popes Emperors and so on but while the Madonna image was frequent in his work with some examples being closely connected to an iconographic tradition some were also reimagined and altered to align with Ramirez's own creativity such as this 1950 placed in an impressive Niche framed by Garland of stylized flowers surrounded by a finely built Arch a woman with blue eyes is looking at us her hands folded as if to pray at first glance we presume we is standing in front of a Madonna but things become less obvious the closer we look for example she has blond's hair which for a Madonna depiction is extremely uncommon she wears a festive but slightly fancy shirt with red stripes and her skirt is elegant behind her we can see a blue sky stars this ignites many questions surrounding the meaning behind this example is she standing is she praying is she laid out as at awake or on the contrary very much alive is she a majestic Madonna or a beautiful American woman decorated with the Stars and Stripes could it be that Ramirez was paying homage to a loved one sadly these are all questions that will likely be left unanswered and left to interpretation yet what this drawing clearly shows is how Ramirez proceeded in his art making he based his work on an established and highly popular model adapted it to fit his own personal purposes bear in mind that this kind of technique is something pretty impressive for an untrained artists to achieve and own this next piece is a personal favorite of mine and also one of the most mysterious pieces in his body of work with the unofficial title of skele it's mysterious not just because of its unknown completion date but also the appearance of a skeleton which to anyone outside of Mexico such as myself first gives off a very grim and Eerie sensation however to Mexicans the image of skeletons and skulls hold a much deeper and more beautifully profound meaning here Ramirez depicts a skeleton playing music which is believed to be a homage to the ancient tradition of Daner d moete or Dance of Death established in the 14th century it was widely popular as a representation of the absolute power of death over human life in contemporary United States and Europe the dance of death was gradually replaced by The Cult of the Eternal Youth and paradoxically found its new subculture in Mexico the dancer Dam as imported by the Spanish conquerors met with the Aztec culture and its Cults this led to a new tradition that found its annual peak in the well-known Day of the Dead where life and death meet in a festive and almost celebratory Gathering where death is not faced with fear and anguish but instead acknowledged as a natural part of life and treated with humor in the lower part of his drawing we see a condensed representation of everyday life cars houses streets and Hills whatever happens the road takes us upward Terrace after Terrace year after year to meet with the Last Dance it seems that Ramirez is betraying death as waiting for us at the summit but it is always present playing its songs on its fiddle sometimes in the background sometimes far away but as always in the close it's hard to say what exactly inspired this imagery perhaps Ramirez was simply once again betraying his culture as a sign of reverence or respect or perhaps for whatever reason he was becoming ever more conscious of death's presence and was prompted to create this drawing but regardless it serves as a useful reminder that death is always present no matter how much we try to ignore it but it shouldn't be regarded as negative or depressing to be conscious of how precious and short our life is can potentially make our lives much more meaningful and with a label of an outsider artist his work offers a front row seat view into a unique visual language one that blends cultural memory personal struggle and an impulse his phenetic lines and reoccurring motifs I think are really themes of displacement resilience and the enduring human spirit Spirit while the circumstances surrounding his art are undeniably tragic Ramirez's Legacy lies in the undeniable power of His Creations his work stands as a testament of a transformative potential of Art in adversity Martin Ramirez may have been an outsider to the traditional art world within his artistic Universe he found a voice of profound Beauty and enduring significance that is truly in one way or another he found his freedom through the confines of a hospital walls through creativity and Imagination that not even his crippling mental health could take away from him thanks items.title: Otto Dix - An Artist of Anguish
items.summary: 19世紀末，當歐洲開始應對衝突和社會動盪的悲慘現實時，一位藝術家從工業化德國的煙囪中崛起，一位藝術家敢於面對人類狀況的原始、不加修飾的真相。奧托·迪克斯是表現主義和新客觀主義運動的大師，也是後來被納粹標記為墮落藝術的藝術風格的關鍵人物，成為藝術勇氣的燈塔。他的作品以對人類痛苦的深層、人類生命的脆弱性、人類的複雜性的內在洞察為標誌。他的藝術旅程是在第一次世界大戰的殘酷、動蕩的魏瑪共和國和拒絕浪漫化或粉飾畫筆作為手術刀的背景下展開的，細緻地剖析了人類的經歷，並揭露了其常常怪誕的弱點。在這段影片中，我們將深入探討奧托·迪克斯的一些最堅定的願景，觀眾面對的不是理想化的英雄或美麗的風景，而是士兵殘破的屍體、窮人的絕望和一個國家在這個災難性時代的道德敗壞。在這裡，我們將深入探討他的作品，從他不和諧的主題到他對戰爭、社會不平等和黑暗的赤裸裸的控訴。到這個頻道，如果您還沒有訂閱，請務必訂閱，點擊通知鈴，以跟上我關於藝術怪異和精彩的一面的更多視頻，大家歡迎來到另一個視頻。今天，我邀請您和我一起探索奧托·迪克斯出生於1891年12月2日的黑暗而具有挑戰性的畫作。他出生在一個相當樸素的家庭，他的父親是鑄鐵廠的模具製造商，迪克斯繼承了他堅強的性格和鋼藍色的眼睛。他從身為裁縫的母親那裡繼承了對音樂和詩歌的熱愛。不出所料，這讓年輕的奧托發現了他的藝術天賦，尤其是繪畫方面的天賦。10歲時，他為畫家弗里茨·阿勒斯曼當模特，他在工作室的經歷給他留下了深刻的印象，他決定在多年後的1906年至1910年間，在當地為迪克斯提供的學徒生涯中，在工藝和技術方面打下了堅實的基礎，磨練了他在油畫和粉彩方面的才能。1909年，迪克斯開始在德勒斯登美術學院學習。在這裡，缺乏嚴格的學術課程，使他能夠探索。特別是，他對古老技術的作品產生了濃厚的興趣，這些技術在他的分層油畫中創造了深度和表現力，受到荷蘭、義大利和學院範圍之外的影響。德勒斯登市充滿活力的藝術場景產生了巨大的創意產出，定期舉辦大型展覽和活動，使他能夠接觸到這些運動的原始情感和大膽的色彩，引起了奧託的共鳴，他開始將它們融入他的作品中。1913年，迪克斯遇到了文森梵谷的色彩藝術和富有表現力的筆觸，這無疑給這位年輕藝術家留下了持久的印象，他已經開始第一次透過出售小型肖像畫和風俗畫以及1914年第一次世界大戰爆發後，迪克斯的生活發生了重大轉折。他熱情地在西部的野戰砲兵團服役。然而，到了第二年，他在戰爭期間目睹的恐怖對權威的懷疑和對權威的懷疑，不用說，這些永遠困擾著他的經歷成為了一個反覆出現的經歷。戰後，迪克斯回到德勒斯登並不受歡迎。奧托·迪克斯（Otto Dix）在魏瑪共和國期間，奧托·迪克斯（Otto Dix）的藝術作品也以赤裸裸的現實主義為特徵，在魏瑪共和國期間，奧托·迪克斯（Otto Dix）的藝術也他對貧困、賣淫等社會弊病進行了嚴厲的批判，毫不退縮地把目光投向了道德和社會不平等。《大都會》描繪的骯髒下流飽受爭議，但這也讓他被任命為德累斯頓學院教授，並隨著納粹黨的崛起而得到認可，迪克斯的藝術受到攻擊。納粹認為他的作品墮落，禁止他展出。他們從博物館的公共收藏中沒收了他的藝術作品，並於1939年第二次世界大戰開始時短暫監禁了他的一些作品。在納粹時代和戰爭最終結束後，奧托·迪克斯的藝術變得更加內省和象徵性。他探索宗教主題，描繪聖經中的場景，並探討死亡和信仰的主題。虽然他后来的作品可能不那么出名，但这反映了艺术家的韧性和不断的探索。在整個20世紀50年代和60年代，他走遍了整個大陸，並不斷展出他的作品。希臘旅行後，他中風，導致左手癱瘓。他後來於1969年去世。自去世以來，奧托·迪克斯仍然是德國最重要的藝術家之一，他對戰爭和社會不公正的堅定描繪繼續引起人們的共鳴。他的作品有力地提醒人們，人類內部可能存在著黑暗，但迪克斯的藝術所代表的持久力量證明了藝術自由的重要性和藝術應對這一問題的責任，這只是一個非常簡短的概述。现在让我们一起深入了解其中一些令人不安的事实。当你翻阅奥托·迪克斯的早期作品时，即使你自认对他的艺术很熟悉，你也可能会遇到不少令人震惊的惊喜。令人著迷的，首先是他當時似乎經常轉向表現主義，粗暴而厚重的繪畫，以及他經常嘗試多種不同的媒介，比如不同的令人震驚的東西，簡單明了，就是他的題材。甚至在他去參加第一次世界大戰之前（這為他後來的作品激發了大量嚴峻的靈感），他這一時期的許多畫作都描繪了令人難以置信的黑暗和圖形主題，甚至他自己也帶有令人毛骨悚然的基調。儘管這些年來他的許多畫作似乎都沒有引起人們的注意，或者也許它們從一開始就沒有引起人們的注意，但在他藝術生涯的這個奇怪的時間框架內，仍然有很多東西需要調查和探索。我想在這段影片中與您一起探索的第一幅畫名為“修女”，完成於1914年。迪克斯在黑暗的立體主義風格背景下描繪了一位孤獨的修女，讓人想起教堂的拱形大廳，或者他呈現修女中心人物的方法遠非帶有尖角的細長形式，並將她的皮膚塗成病態的綠色，而她嘴周圍和眼睛下方的紅色斑塊給人一種她生病或生病的印象。儘管她臉上的表情有些平靜，但她的表情卻在腐爛，這對我來說造成了一種非常不安的情緒衝突。在她身後的混亂和腐爛的皮膚中，她平靜的微笑傳達了一種接受厄運的狀態，或者可能是無知或否認的狀態。這是早期優先考慮情感影響的一個標誌，奧托·迪克斯也融入了立體主義元素，特別是在他的早期。為了更補充我們談到的面對厄運的幸福否認的概念，他的分裂可能像徵著信仰的分裂或處於混亂邊緣的世界。考慮到這幅畫的日期是1914年，畫中的其他一些物體往往會吸引你的注意力，時間越長，在左邊，一個輻射狀的陰戶形狀的形式將十字架上痛苦的血淋淋的耶穌推到一邊，上面有一個似乎非常大的王冠。這幅畫中讓我有點困惑的一個元素是右手邊的一個孕婦。這是否也反映了藝術家在戰爭邊緣的焦慮？也許是對現在註定要發生的事情的恐懼，對未來幾代人的未來的恐懼。很難確定，但這似乎是我的印象。考慮到據報道，奧托·迪克斯在參戰時非常熱情，我的這個理論可能與藝術家當時對戰爭的感受截然不同。還有一個問題是這幅畫是否涉及誘惑的主題。這位修女是否會受到強烈的誘惑，拋棄她對基督的忠誠，現在被推到了左上角，屈服於她的性慾，成為一名母親，正如外陰和女性的主導符號所暗示的那樣？一如既往，我很想聽聽你對這些畫作的想法。如果你有更好的想法，請在評論中告訴我其他人。不管怎樣，我發現這幅畫令人著迷，有形而華麗，有著令人難以忘懷的調色板，與他目前收藏在紐約市現代藝術博物館的《修女》相比，這是一個相當突出的概念，這是戰爭的第一個恐怖，可以肯定地說，這種影響嚴重滲透到雖然只是這個時期的許多例子中的一個，但當年完成的《垂死的戰士》似乎是最重要的角色之一。這幅暴力而生動的畫作確實是對第一次世界大戰噩夢般現實的令人震驚的描繪，將觀眾帶入大屠殺的中心。呈現給我們的是一個孤獨的士兵躺在戰場上毫無生氣的樣子。他曾經引以為傲的製服現在變成了泥土和血跡的怪誕混合物。他的臉因無聲的尖叫而扭曲，表現出痛苦、迪克斯使用粗糙油漆層、士兵身體上的痛苦以及戰爭的非人性影響的令人痛苦的混合。曾經驕傲的士兵會變得支離破碎、面目全非。將戰鬥描繪得充滿了優雅的浪漫主義氣息，彷彿在美化戰鬥中的打架行為。奧托·迪克斯的藝術作品中的這些概念早已不復存在。《垂死的戰士》強化了戰爭造成的徹底破壞。相反，呈現的是一片荒涼的荒原，充滿了泥土、血和火。鮮血中沒有英雄氣概和光榮的痕跡，柔和的綠色和棕色，進一步渲染了場景的淒涼，畫作確實是對戰爭慘痛代價的有力控訴。這件作品中的表現主義技巧將觀眾直接推向了現實，雖然難以理解，但它強烈地提醒人們，士兵們在苦難中所付出的代價。這件作品是對戰爭的持久表達，敦促觀眾面對魯莽和魯莽勇敢的代價。下一幅名為「艾利斯」的畫作於1919年完成，是一種相當令人不安但又耐人尋味的表現主義肖像畫風格，我總是發現自己會回來看它。我所能掌握的資訊非常有限。這幅畫描繪了一位身著傳統服裝的陌生女子，她似乎有一頭棕色短髮，不祥地融入了她那雙銳利的眼睛，帶著相當險惡的微笑，所有這些似乎都隱藏在面紗的微妙外觀後面。這再次與她優雅的衣服和美麗的花朵所顯示的美麗產生了一種不安的衝突。恐怕我必須承認，我無法找到太多資訊來說明是什麼讓這張肖像對我來說如此有趣，而我為什麼想將它包含在這段影片中，是因為不太了解這個女人是誰，也不知道這個故事是什麼，艾利斯對藝術家來說是陌生人還是她是情人？正如我們稍後將在本視頻中了解到的那樣，奧托·迪克斯（Otto 迪克斯在該藝術家的教學職位，這是他另一幅最著名的諷刺畫作的催化劑，該畫作於1933年完成，被稱為《七大罪》。這幅油畫和蛋彩畫並不是對當時允許法西斯主義蓬勃發展的社會和政治氣候的毫無歉意的批評。這幅畫描繪了一群怪誕的人物，每個人物都體現了一種致命的罪惡。例如，中間描繪的懶惰或懶惰的形像是一個拿著鐮刀跳舞的骷髏形象，使社會弊病惡化。如果你仔細觀察，你甚至可能會發現他的姿勢是像徵性的，他伸出的雙臂和鐮刀形成了納粹標誌。左下角那個瘦削、駝背的老婦人被認為代表了她背上棲息的一個微小的白色人物，由於他戴著面具，戰後還增加了鬍子，所以經常被解釋為希特勒，原來留著更多的鬍子。這個人物據說代表嫉妒、吞噬和騎乘。在右手邊，我們看到背景中一個狂躁、狂暴的角怪物，似乎代表憤怒。巨大、腫脹的頭部，耳朵被堵住，一些觀察家認為它的嘴是肛門，代表了虛榮的罪惡。這讓我們看到了虛榮旁邊的人物，一個戴著黏土面具、張大嘴巴的胖臉人物，可能代表了戰後的嫉妒形象，似乎有非常清楚和可以理解的原因，因為你對這位藝術家的生平研究越多，就添加了希特勒面具。希特勒，新政府，最有可能的是，任何危險的提及都是收件人摧毀的原因唯一的信息來源是他的搜查和解僱後，迪克斯和他的家人離開了屬於他的舊城堡的村莊居住他向藝術品經銷商借錢買了爐子和導電，並開始創造中性風景，微笑的女孩和鮮花以賺取一些收入《七大罪》中跳舞的骷髏被描繪成這樣的位置，他的衣服圖案形成了一個藝術家後來說，這譴責了他的同胞的懶惰和被動，這導致了這幅畫的主角當然是嫉妒，牢牢佔據並統治著它，最小的，微不足道的，但最重要的罪惡戴著面具。在第一幅草圖中，很明顯，很容易透過鬍鬚辨識出來。迪克斯拿著照片，不敢描繪這個細節，因為這與肖像畫太相似了。小鬍子的畫作並不是在第二次世界大戰結束後，沒有什麼可以阻止藝術家畫出這最後兩筆。考慮到這一點，《七宗罪》是一部非常重要的歷史傳記，我們在他的信件之外記錄了藝術家當時的感受，而這些信件經常被納粹截獲。它強烈提醒人們不受控制的惡習和批評納粹政權的危險，即使帶有隱藏的象徵意義，也證明了藝術向人們說出真相的力量。隔年的1934年，隨著第二次世界大戰迫在眉睫的威脅的逼近，奧托·迪克斯繼續在他的作品中發表強有力的政治聲明，儘管他在這一年完成的一幅這樣的畫作不僅探討了生活本身的恐怖，題為《遺憾的是，《再次的勝利》與他的其他作品相比並沒有那麼多。只要快速瀏覽一下這幅畫，我們就可以看到我們一生中經歷的不同階段，這些階段主要是從藝術家的角度來講述的。在右邊，我們可以看到一個年輕人的象徵意義變得明顯，當我們看到他們面前的地上有一個無辜的幼兒時，使這些人物中的每一個都代表我們的孩子上面是一個正在做家務的女僕，而她上面是一個驕傲的人也許這兩個人物再次代表了德國大多數同齡人的典型成年生活的集體象徵。似乎也注意到了，這就是統治和可怕。骷髏人物揮舞著鐮刀，很像典型的死神描繪，頭戴王冠，象徵著他可怕的統治，正如畫名所暗示的那樣，無處可藏，所有出生的人都是注定的。老人和他的狗似乎是唯一注意到死亡的人，也許表明，當我們到了老年，我們越來越意識到死亡的雖然有趣的是，死亡之刃的尺寸似乎幾乎完全纏繞在士兵的脖子上。也許這可以代表那些自豪地走進戰場的士兵的完全無視的立場使這個概念變得更加悲慘，因為他認為自己很可能將他描繪成除了對死亡的現實一無所知，而且他的畫作離他有多近，納粹禁止展出這幅畫，在某種程度上，它代表了奧托·迪克斯本人可能在地平線上看到的另一種死亡，那就是他的死亡。在這幅畫完成的同年，他被迫加入在第二次世界大戰的最後十年裡，他所剩下的一點創作自由只會越來越少，直到戰爭正式開始時最終被自己的同胞監禁。1939年，宣戰和德國士兵入侵歐洲各地的聲音猛烈迴響，第二次世界大戰現在已經開始。至於奧托·迪克斯，納粹政權的偏執在這段時間得到了極大的凸顯，迪克斯因涉嫌為藝術家策劃低谷而被短暫監禁，他的許多畫作被毀，在戰爭過程中幾乎沒有任何新作品出現，突顯了他在納粹統治下面臨的始終存在的威脅。然而，在此期間，他也完成了可以說是他作為藝術家最成熟的作品之一，題為《紅幕前的調色板自畫像》，完成於1942年。在這個場景中，他直接面向觀眾，而在其他肖像中，當他從事自己的行為時，可以看到窗外阿爾卑斯山的黑暗和不祥的景色。这种选择将艺术家非常温暖的环境与背景中的外部世界末日世界结合起来，很可能突显了他当时的精神状态。藝術似乎是他唯一的避難所，即使外面的世界似乎一片混亂，充滿了衝突和破壞，藝術也從未離開過他的身邊。這位藝術家很快就被徵召入伍。他在战争结束时被法国人俘虏并被关押。不要浪費時間，他很快就會注意到藝術風格的轉變，非常讓人想起他最早的作品。这一时期的画作，直到他去世前的最后几幅画，似乎再次更倾向于表现主义，颜料层厚，更超现实。这些画作很多都集中在战后苦难、宗教寓言和圣经场景等主题上。1949年题为《复活》的画作似乎代表着基督从他的作品中浮现出来。至少在我看來，他這一時期最奇怪的畫作之一是他1946年的畫作，題為《調色板是黑暗而柔和的，增強了這幅畫的嚴峻情緒，喚起了一種死亡感。偶爾閃現的紅色可能像徵著血腥、暴力或廢墟的面具》這個標題是我們向世界呈現的一個強大的外觀，但在這裡它們被打破了，這些面具的面孔可以被視為代表那些經歷過戰爭的人支離破碎的身份。他1948年的畫作《Ecce Homo》，其肖像位於鐵絲網後面，在這裡，藝術家描繪了自己在鐵絲網後面，全身生瘡，坐在自己的尿液中，這是監禁和壓迫的有力像徵。標題Ecce Homo是拉丁語，意為“看那人”，是本丟彼拉多在《聖經》中所說的一句話當奧托·迪克斯在他的面前向人群展示耶穌基督時，奧托·迪克斯將自己融入到場景中，將基督的苦難與納粹迫害者的苦難以及更廣泛的等同破壞起來。奧托·迪克斯最終回到了德累斯頓，在那裡一直待到1966年。在此期間，在當時分裂的德國兩地，對他作品的認可度再次開始上升。1959年，他被授予德意志聯邦共和國大功勳十字勳章。1950年，他被提名為國家獎，但未能成功。他在漢堡獲得了Lichtwark獎，在德累斯頓獲得了馬丁·安德森·內克瑟藝術獎，以紀念他75歲。同年，他獲得了漢斯·托馬獎，隨後又被授予了“倫勃朗獎”。1968年，他在薩爾斯堡獲得了歌德基金會的倫勃朗獎。在1969年去世之前，他完成了一幅《瑪塞拉》，據我所知，是他的孫女之一，似乎在他生命的最後幾年裡，奧托·迪克斯已經擺脫了戰爭和不公正的邪惡本質，轉向了他所尋求的更加豐富和健康的幸福。1965年完成的一幅早期畫作描繪了瑪塞拉和他的另一個孫女娜娜在花園裡。我在lamperts.com上看到的一篇關於這件作品的文章完美地詳細介紹了奧托·迪克斯在他的作品中所採用的技術，“在色彩和繪畫形式中發現的樂趣，以及在大而發光的紙張上實現的平版印刷術的重新發現，都是他的典型特徵，從他的水洗技術到細節的全部原始清晰度，沒有計算形式化的理想構圖，沒有明確的目標改變的基礎上定義了他的作品。似乎在他最後的日子裡，他不再希望探索黑暗，而是專注於他的幸福和他的幸福。在這個國家的戰場和街頭承受瞭如此多的痛苦之後，這個國家不僅幻滅了他，壓迫了他，拋棄了他，囚禁了他，他可能突然而意外地死去，但並沒有。令人欣慰的是，他留下的黑暗和飽受戰爭蹂躪的形象並不是他唯一的遺產，儘管它們如此重要和令人大開眼界，但他也留下了一份溫柔他靈魂的一部分可以在這些最終的創作中得到見證，給我們一個額外寶貴的教訓，那就是永遠不要讓生命的黑暗使者完全主宰我們，即使死亡使者我們，而是用我們心中的愛，而是用我們心中的愛，非常感謝您的觀看。你發現這個影片內容豐富，我希望你渴望探索更多這個極為重要的作品。一如既往，很遺憾我不能在這個影片中包含更多他的畫作，但不要讓這阻止你探索他的藝術之旅。這個影片更多的是給你一個起點來觀察我在這個頻道上介紹的藝術家的畫作，但重要的是一如既往地有你，我期待在下面閱讀你自己的解釋。在我離開之前，我想花點時間分享一些我可愛的觀眾在我的影片結尾發送給我的一些藝術作品。今天的特色獎金藝術家是瓦倫丁，一位局外人藝術家，他在中學時用筆名朋克搖滾鬼魂更加勤奮。年底離開學校的一位藝術老師注意到了他，儘管他從未上過課，只在午餐和空閒時間在房間裡閒逛，並給了他一大堆另一本，允許學生用任何材料自由創作。這段時間讓他開始使用壓克力繪畫，發現顏料確實推進了他的進步之旅。他自己的風格是一種逃避的東西，靈感和影響激發了他對藝術的熱愛和創造力，如文森特·梵高、皮埃爾·波納爾、卡拉瓦喬、弗里達·卡羅、愛德華·霍珀、詹姆斯·恩索爾和雷內·馬格里特，只是為了直接引用他自己對自己作品的反思，引用，“我覺得我的作品總是以不合時宜的方式結束，但唉，它最終成為我的手繼續結束的東西，我的目標是試著對我來說，繪畫中最重要的元素之一是色彩世界，我發現我越來越多地嘗試用我手頭上的工具和顏料來翻譯它，我什至用一把尺子和一根縫紉針自己製作了一些用於精確細節工作的工具。瓦倫丁的第一個官方系列名為《歌謠》，他在其中解釋說，他正在大力描繪場景。他告訴我，他一直想畫那些文藝復興時期的畫作，其中所有的人物都在一起講述一個故事。例如，他的畫作《舞蹈》是一種情感，他最終不得不開始這樣做，在他個人知道瓦倫丁想到這些之後，他會說否則。「我只是唯一一個必須用繪畫來講述我希望講述的故事的模特，我目前正在創作迄今為止最大、最複雜的作品，以聖母憐子圖為主題，我情不自禁地與瓦倫丁有很多共同點，他認為我也發現自己被周圍的色彩所吸引，並在其中看到了很多可以激發出如此深刻的東西，這就是為什麼我像磁石一樣被他的藝術所吸引，尤其是當看到他如何完美地將這些色調融合在一起，創造出如此超凡脫俗的厚重作品時，有紋理的油漆層投入瞭如此多的關注和關注，我覺得這確實強調了他對媒介的掌握。我認為他在這裡可以提供一些真正獨特的東西，如果您能去查看更多內容，這對我來說意義重大。請透過您在螢幕上看到的連結前往他的Instagram，或點擊描述中的連結向他展示一些內容。如果您也是藝術家，並且希望有可能出現在即將發布的影片中，請向我發送一封電子郵件，其中包含有關您和您的藝術的描述以及您的作品範例，或在Instagram上向我發送訊息。最後，我要向一直以來支持Patreon和頻道會員選項卡的用戶表示衷心的感謝。在此向我所有的頂級Carol H和Charlie Sanchezy致敬。今天的內容就到此為止了。

items.title: The Dark World of Odilon Redon
items.summary: the work of French artist odilon redon regarded as one of the most important original symbolists of the late 19th early 20th centuries defies easy categorization his work transcends the movements blending elements of symbolism surrealism and even hints of imp impressionism through his exploration of Dreams imagination and the subconscious redon is most well known for his body of monochromatic artwork that exploited the expressive and suggested powers of the color black known as the Noir series although many other more colorful works of his would be just as compelling and unsettling it is his Sinister black charcoal Noir drawings that seem to tap deep into the Curiosity of many art enthusiast when they hear the name of odilon redon primarily for their intimate connection to the Hidden Side of Ron's mind that he would creatively willingly put on display for viewers experience in this video we will delve into that very same experience together by taking a close look at some of redon's Most Fascinating pieces within his Noir series to unravel the Mysteries that lie within many of the strange bring to life whether depicting Landscapes or ethereal figures many compositions of his within this morbidly alluring series invite us to embark on a journey of pure introspection and contemplation but since his talent transcends his use of charcoal alone particularly in his later work we also be taking a quick look at some of his other paintings and pastel drawings as well as I feel there is still much that we can explore within his more abstract vibrant World which he created alongside his darker work his ability to go beyond the confines of reality and evoke a sense of wonder continued to inspire generations of artists and art fans alike including me someone who loves to create art with charcoal and pastel myself who regards him as a very big influence as well as some viewers on this channel who I noticed suggested that I cover this artist someday and I guess now is that time please be sure to subscribe and hit the notification Bell for more videos from me on the weird and wonderful side of the art world and of course welcome to another video my friends join me as we embark on a journey into the mystical Realms of redon's imagination where the boundaries between the conscious and the subconscious blur and the mysteries of odilon redon born bertran Jean redon on April 20th 1840 in Bordeaux France was raised in a cultured bouro family the wealth of his family ripened from rather unfortunate Roots however as his father made his fortune through the slave trades in Louisiana during the 1830s redon initially pursued a career in architecture studying briefly under Jean Leon Bona in Paris however his true passion lay in the realm of art showing fine promise at drawing at a young age he soon abandoned architecture to dedicate himself fully to creating art redon's early Artistic Endeavors were influenced by The Works of romantic and symbolist movements as well as by his encounters with the literary and philosophical occurrence of his time he etching developing a distinctive style characterized by a delicate balance between light and Shadow and an emphasis on imaginative subject matter in the 1870s after returning from his service in the Franco Prussian War until its end in 1871 redon work meticulously in refining his style he eventually began to gain recognition for his series of charcoal drawings known as the noirs which depicted Fantastical and often macb imagery inspired by his dreams and inner Visions by the 1880s these Works attracted the attention of influential writers and artists including jolis car huisman who championed Ron's unique artistic Vision including his drawings his cult novel titled Aro or against English throughout his career redon continued to evolve as an artist experimenting with color and form in his later pastol and oil pieces his imagery ranged from Haunting Landscapes and mysterious figures to Vivid depictions of flowers and other natural elements all imbued with a sense of Otherworldly Beauty and mystery by the beginning of a 1900s after seemingly abandoning his dark and Moody charcoal drawings Al together for more abstract paintings recognized with numerous exhibitions and accolades including the Legion of Honor in 1903 and the salon D dor in 1904 despite his growing reputation redon remained a private and let his art speak for itself rather than notoriety and it was around this time that another curious development in his style began to emerge which was his Keen interest in Hinduism and Buddhism as well as their cultures which increasingly showed in his work most notably his piece titled the Buddha completed in 1905 which features what appears to be the Japanese interpretation of the Buddha of infinite light and life named amitaba the central Buddha of devotion within the pure land sect of Buddhism that flourished as the new century continued odilon passed away on July 6th 1916 leaving behind a legacy that continues to inspire and Intrigue artists and art enthusiasts around the world his exploration of inner depths of a human psyche and his ability to evoke a sense of wonder and mystery through his art ensure that his work remains as relevant and captivating today as it was first I'd like us to take a look at one of his earlier pieces within his Noir collection titled Guardian Spirit of the 1878 this charcoal composition seems to grab the viewers attention immediately with what could only be described as a large head of in the sky above a calm ocean with equally large yet downwards towards a sailboat with surrounding goals flitting about and waves the sea stretches far out to a featureless horizon presenting us with vastness if you look closer you can just about make out a delicate looking Halo that surrounds the head as well as what appears to be a wing on the far left given this strange head a character of being Angelic or like a Divine being whilst also maintaining a degree of ominous domination over the environment below according to One Source I came across when the artist's father Bernard redon was a young man he traveled from France to Louisiana in order to try and recoup the family's lost wealth that he had accumulated in the slave train while there he met and married redon's mother odil on their later return to France odil was pregnant with odilo who Bordeaux the artist often regretted that he was not born at Sea an environment that odilon himself described as quote a place without a country on an abyss with this in mind perhaps this work could be seen as representing a kind of alternative birth for Lon perhaps the large head in the sky is actually a self-portrait of his destined or even desired emergence into the world as he always envisioned it's of course hard to say for sure but the strange foreshadows a surrealist style that throughout the 20th century in which such imagery invites the viewer to ask this as for the technical aspects of this piece the drawing is very typical of redon's noirs in which he manipulated the charcoal Medium as well as merely applying it to paper in order to achieve the array of tones and textures that we can see such techniques that he would Master included wiping stumping smudging even adding touches of chalk to highlights most notably around the eye of a head facing a viewer which seems to have a distin inve glowing ring around it as if caught in the light beam of the sun which again emphasizes the Heavenly benevolent aura that seems to emanate from this being watching quietly above this next piece which I consider to be one of his most gripping when I first saw it is simply titled Apparition with a slightly uncertain completion 1890 this would in fact be one of other artworks that shared this title which included his later piece under the same name completed in 1910 featuring an abstract floral display and two ghostly white figures walking down a hazy staircase on the right presenting both a mysterious atmosphere accompanied by a disorientating Cascade of color in this earlier work though the atmosphere is nothing short of sheer threat and Dread there are heavy deposits of charcoal spread across the paper like Black Rain with the mysterious face of a bearded man peering through on the right with dark sunken eyes the ambiguity of a figure's identity and significance is one of the most striking aspects of its work is it a ghost a spirit or simply a this open to interpretation inviting viewers to emoke moods and emotions rather than trying to depict a concrete subject there is again though a slight strange element of divine energy that seems to emanate from this figure at least for me perhaps it's just the beard expression on his face in spite of of a dark chaos around him but he almost appears to look like Jesus Christ which when looking at other examples of rayon's work even within other Noir drawings depictions of Christ would not be a stranger to his collection regardless of the exact identity the figure's ghostly appearance suggests a presence from Beyond the realm of living hinting at themes of mortality spirituality and the unknown Ron was deeply influenced by the writings and imagery used within the short stories of Edgar alen Poe and other Gothic writers whose themes would often leak into the work of radons furthermore the composition of apparition adds to its enigmatic atmosphere the figure is positioned slightly off center creating a sense of imbalance and tension the use of negative space and Shadow further emphasizes the Eerie mood drawing the viewer's Gaze towards a mysterious figure at the edge of a work with the darkness and Shadow also being a key character in itself alongside the figure through its dreamlike imagery Supernatural atmosphere the drawing is a prime example of redon's invitation to viewers to explore the depths of their own imagination and subconscious making it both a haunting display but a the next charcoal drawing is titled cactus man completed between 1881 and 1882 the drawing to picks a man's head emerging from a decorative Square flower pot the head itself is also covered in menacing looking spikes resembling that cactus his expression seems to be one of observation with large somewhat dull eyes and full lips the flower pot although quite tricky to make out is decorated with an image of an Amazon slaying a man referencing the Greek myth of his female warriors whose conflation of feminine and masculine traits poetically Echoes Circ conflation of human and plant forms presented to us in drawing although again it is open to personal perspective I can't help but get the impression that this drawing presenting the merge of human and plant perception of boundaries between the human world and the natural world this blurring could represent a connection to Nature a vulnerability to its harshness or perhaps a potential for growth and resilience the cactus spikes emerging from the man's head evoke for suffering of Christ's Crown of Thorns suggesting themes of sacrifice endurance and the potential for beauty to emerge from Pain the image of the Amazon on the flower pot known for their strength and Defiance of traditional gender roles jux opposes for seemingly passive portrayal of a man this could be interpreted as a commentary on the societal expectations of masculinity or a broader exploration of gender fluidity in addition perhaps the figure solitary confinement in the partt and his large observant eyes introspection and a silent awareness of a world around him one other interpretation I came across which I found quite surprising explores the potential influence of redon's exposure to an exhibition showcasing the indigenous people of Tiara def go an archipelago at the southernmost tip of South America who had a profound if not complicated impact on the artist and whom he described as being quote hay grotesque on the one hand he also reportedly admired the Purity and simplicity of a so-called primitive people while on the other hand he recognized them as the Fearsome Origins with with a decorative flower pot a symbol of Western culture and containment Ron's hybrid cactus man can be understood as an attempt to reconcile the two poles of human existence nature and culture wild and civilized but of course and I can't stress this enough the complexities of such an interpretation require careful sensitivity it's important to remember that this was an artist whose father was a slave trader during a very different time in history to today where many Europeans had a rather shall we say warped view of native people so if we're going to take an interpretation like this into account it's vital to understand the circumstances and nature of Ron's generation and upbringing in any case by examining the various symbols and their potential meanings cactus man allows us to delve into the themes of human connection to Nature the complexities of human experience and the power of art to evoke emotions and contemplation next we have the charcoal 1882 titled the eye like a strange Infinity it is the first plate from a 10-part series titled aned Capo once again inspired by The Works of the po the artwork features a single disembodied eye morphed into a strange shape of a hot air balloon it's upward gazing Iris and pupil resembling a dark dark pulsating void the eye is depicted as detached from its owner floating freely against a hazy background of clouds instead of a basket containing passengers the balloon carries what looks like a severed head on a platter much like that of St John the Baptist in the biblical story of Salon in the lower left the FRS of a lonely palm-like plant are appearing Out of the Shadows the central eye is often interpreted as a symbol of a human mind specifically aspects from my personal point of view this disembodied nature might suggest a separation from the physical world delving into the Realms of Dreams introspection the many faint ropes attaching to the eye can be seen as between the conscious and an unconscious mind or the fragile nature of human perception the balloon-like quality of the eye might further suggest a sense of Ascension or the desire of journeying referencing the vastness of the human psyche or the mysteries of the universe the Cloudy backgrounds adds to the dreamlike and ethereal quality of the artwork the eyeball disassociated from the physical body could be seen as a symbol for freedom from the constraints of everyday life and the attainment of a Consciousness according to scholar and Creator jod hunman quote floating up towards Infinity let loose from the limitations of body and mind Ron's eyes are free to really see beyond reality Beyond nature beyond the visible end the connection to edar Alan Poe is also significant Po's work often explored themes of Darkness the Supernatural and the exploration of a human psyche these themes resonate with the symbolist elements presented in radon's artwork the eyes unsettling gaze and its Journey towards Infinity evoke a sense of mystery introspection and the potential for encountering the unknown that mirrors the introspective and often writing overall this artwork truly is imagery it delves into the complexities of a human mind and invites viewers to consider the vastness of the Unseen and next we have redon's infinite search 1886 a lithograph that captures yet more elements in this work the dominating image is that of a figure with strands of straw-like hair and exaggerated facial features overlooking what looks like some kind of chalice emitting Vapor or smoke that climbs to the ceiling of an ancient looking room almost reminiscent of a medieval castle or a church this figure to me almost resembles a witch experimenting with Alchemy in the dead of night she appears to be in a state of contemplation focusing on the Chalice or perhaps searching for something intangible as suggested by the title The Infinite search the figure's elongated form warped facial features and sinuous Contours evoke a sense of movement and transformation suggesting a state of metamorphosis as is typical of Ron's work that we've already seen symbolism plays a significant role in the infinite search the nocturnal setting and the figure solitary Journey evoke a sense of existential angst and the Quest for meaning in the face of mystery the mysterious leaving more questions and answers and a complex Melting Pot of moods it wouldn't surprise me though if this was exactly what redon intended let's now take a look at one of drawings the 1887 piece simply tied spider the drawing features a rather large spider with a fuzzy looking body 10 legs instead of the usual eight it most striking feature is its very humanlike facial features consisting of a snub nose and a wide smiling mouth that reveals a row of tiny white teeth creating a strange and paradoxical image from the way the spider is tilted it gives off the impression that the spider is descending from a thread of its web from the ceiling down to what looks like floor much like the images of Christ spiders have appeared before in his work with equally bizarre blends of arachnet human features Ron based this particular print upon an earlier charcoal drawing but the lithographic medium which uses greasy ink or crayon applied directly to a smooth Stone was equally well suited to the artist exploration of the color black for me I immediately get the sense that the spider with its additional legs and human smile suggests a creature from the realm of Dreams nightmares or the subconscious the smile a symbol of joy friendliness just opposed with the spider a creature often associated with fear and danger creates an interesting Duality this reflects the complexities of human nature and the potential for both good and evil within us the spider might represent hidden fears or anxieties that lurk beneath the surface of our Consciousness or perhaps himself the act of drawing it out and giving it form even a seemingly playful one could be a way for ridon to confront these fears much like the cactus man this work blurs the lines between the natural world that being The Spider and the human world with its humanlike smile this reflects a common theme in symbolism where artists explored the imaginative and subjective experience of reality to create an image that is totally Fantastical it comes to little surprise that raidon was reportedly fascinated with the Natural Sciences and with the encouragement of his friend the botanist arong clev he studied Anatomy oology and microscopic life he also frequently visited paris's Museum of Natural History which included exhibits of biological abnormalities and he even lectures it seems that many of these beasts and monsters that appear in his work could well have been based on observation but were mutated by his imagination The Smiling spider serves as a wonderful recognition of our Humanity in these strange hybrid creatures the almost inherent human fear of spiders mixed with the playful grin of a fuzzy spider makes images like this both appealing and unsettling at the same time another unnerving example of r On's Noir is titled before I saw the vaporous Contours of a human form another 1896 like an image straight out of a ghost story this piece is incredibly chilling interestingly enough this image was in fact used as part of a series inspired by a ghost story The Haunted the haunters by Edward bullwood Litton leaving us with some confidence supernatural the title itself Sparks curiosity it hints at a mysterious Vision a revelation where a human form emerges from something undefined it may even be a direct quote and experience of himself the central image is a white hazy and wispy form that suggests a human figure is not a clear impressionistic blur the figure sits in a dark room where we can see in the background two staring eyes gazing towards us and the figure from the darkness which leaves us with a puzzling uncomfortable question is the ghost the seated hazy figure in front or is it the eyes that we can see in the shadows without a doubt many of rayon's Noir drawings capture the most Intrigue within the vast collection of his artwork but there are still some wonderful examples of his more colorful work that capture the same level of Fascination so for the rest of this video I'd like us to take a look at some of rayon's pastel and oil paintings to not only observe his versatility as an artist but also explore the same degree of mystery that he accomplishes Within for example his piece titled figure 1876 interestingly seems to almost capture the same themes and moods as this first piece we looked at Guardian waters we're once again presented with a large head suspended in the air with the aid of angel-like wings against a beautiful setting all Rising Sun behind it is an elegant woman who seems to be holding the disembodied head with the ease of drying and washing the orange glowing sun behind feels similarly omnipotent the way it seems to fill the entire background puts an end to any sense of the outward exterior perspective unlike guardian of a spirit Waters the expression of a head in Earthly Simplicity Contours Stern and strong as the holder's own face is scrolled with an alarming shity the head gazes off beyond the image to elsewhere she is not concerned with the situation suggests that neither should you be rather the real Marvel here is the palet of figure it's drying radiating heat that folds over the image with a wicked Hue below the duo a crispy Bracken Falls seemingly glowing from within with an quote oron red on stag from 1900 is a captivating exploration of the inner World while the pastel drawing defies contribute to its dreamlike atmosphere symbolic meaning the central figure is a woman with flowing dark hair her eyes in a state of serene contemplation her ghostly form suggests an ethereal presence existing beyond the confines of a physical world she appears to reside within a boundless cloudy space rendered in a soft pallet of Blues Reds and yellows further emphasizing the everchanging and unsolid quality of daydreaming her relaxed and almost again a state of introspection where the blur the absence of a defined background allows a viewer to project their own interpretations and emotions onto the music believing it held the key to unlocking the depths of a human psyche he saw rat as a visual manifestation of the emotions and experiences evoked by music while Daydream doesn't depict any literal musical elements the swirling forms and soft colors evoke a sense of Harmony and flow reminiscing of a soundscape this connection is further strengthened by Ron's own writings where he expressed the limitations of color in capturing the essence of Music which he experience as we'll see in the next piece titled parul completed in 1912 even within redon's work that included color dark and morbid themes would still occasionally creep up to the surface with a similar yet Bleaker style to that of Daydream this gripping image of a solitary figure up against a lonely mountainous landscape is believed to be inspired by Vagner 3 Act 1882 Opera under the same name inspired by The Legend of a Holy Grail where on revisits the theme of his early ol lithograph 1892 in this version though redon's paral deviates significantly from the typical portrayals here the warrior has been stripped of his armor his helmet Lance transformed into a more introspective figure perhaps Aus a wise man or Seer this is evident in his solitary pose and the contemplative isolation the background is Stark featuring bare mountains rendered in somber tones of violet and black this internal State one devoid of comfort or items.summary: it almost begs belief when looking through the paintings of Eve tongi that such perfect technique of dramatic lighting and shadows cold atmospheres such organic looking imagery could be achieved by an artist that had little to no formal training in art whatsoever stepping into a painting by Eve tongi is akin to traversing the threshold of a dream ape where biomorphic shapes morph into impossible Landscapes bathed in an unsettling yet strangely alluring light his canvases imbued with the spirit of surrealism transport us to the Realms where logic surrenders to the Fantastical and the Supreme to analyze Toni's art is to embark on a voyage of Discovery ambiguous forms each whispering imagination in this video we will delve into the captivating world of some of their unique visual language and exploring the artistic influences that shape them we will journey through recurring themes in his work such as the interplay between vastness and intimacy the unsettling beauty of Decay and the enigmatic presence of Shadows we will Auto examine tongi relationship with the surrealist movement analyzing how his individual voice resonated with the subconscious don't forget to subscribe hit the notification Bell to see more videos from me on the weird and wonderful side of art welcome to another video everyone and prepared to be bewildered intrigued and perhaps even challenged as we navigate through the born on the 5th of January 1900 in Paris Eve Toni's life like his paintings unfolded in a series of dramatic forms tragedy would strike him and his family from an early age with his father dying in 1908 and his brother being killed during the first world war as as he Grew Older he gravitated towards the sea spending time on Merchant ships and later finding inspiration in its vastness and mystery in 1920 he was conscripted into the French army in Tunis where he met the poet Shak PR who was apparently amused by Toni's eccentric and strange habits from chewing his socks to eating live spiders the latter became a party trick that he it was a vibrant partisan art scene during this decade that truly began to shift him towards the art World a life-changing encounter with the georgo 1923 sparked Toni's artistic Journey drawn to the surrealist movement's exploration of a subconscious and the irrational he quickly found himself surrounded by the likes of Andre Breton mcgr despite having no formal training t I's Unique Style blossomed characterized shapes Barren Landscapes bathed in ethereal light and a sense of suspended animation his paintings with titles like indefinite divisibility for example or through Birds through fire but not through glass invited viewers to abandon conventional logic and delve into forms he became a key figure in gaining critical Acclaim for his 1939 Love Led tongi across the Atlantic where he met and married fellow artist case Sage who shared a relatively similar style to tongi and who I think May in fact also be worth exploring on someday settling in Connecticut tongi continue to paint prolifically finding inspiration in the American landscape while retaining his distinct European influence style during World War II he became a vocal advocate for exiled artists and participated in exhibitions alongside other European surrealists who sought refuge in the United States Toni's influence extended beyond the art World inspiring filmmakers like Alfred Hitchcock and other famous surrealists like Salvador Dar despite Toni remained humble and dedicated to his craft sadly he passed away in 1955 after suffering a fatal stroke leaving behind a rich Legacy of paintings that continue to Captivate and the first painting we'll be looking at today is titled mama papa is wounded 1927 one of Toni's earliest masterpieces this work invites both admiration and perplexity his enigmatic unrelated objects demands more than a fleeting glance so let's try looking deeper and unveil the layers of of meaning hidden within it dominating the canvas is a vast empty space bathed in an eerie grayish violet light this Dio's work casts long ominous Shadows contributing to an overall sense of unease the barren desert-like terrain evokes a post-apocalyptic Wasteland a world stripped of comfort and scattered across a desolate landscape are several curious objects seemingly defying conventional logic a looming cactus-like form Tethered to a webike structure appears neither fully free or imprisoned what appear to be what could only be described as beans or Pebbles are scattered in different locations in the landscape casting dramatic Shadows onto the ground a tall trunk or stalk of a plant covered in spikes appears on the right with an ominous dark black mass behind it which looks like smoke or a raincloud there is also what looks like the shape of a torso that lies abandoned on the trunk of spikes is also a subtle sight of a green string wrapped around it giving off the impression of a snake winding itself around a branch in the distance there is a strange pale pole that winds and bends seems to be disintegrating into the wind next to it almost appears like the shape of a ghost emerging from the ground with two dark Bey contribute to the painting's Dreamlight quality further blurring the lines imagination adding to the Enigma is the evocative title mama papa is wounded does it reference an actual event a primal fear or perhaps a collective Society given its open-ended nature the interpretations due to what we already know of his beloved Fallen brother some see it as a reflection of the anxiety violence that followed World War I whilst others perceive a Freudian desires Accord according to one Theory I came across the yellow figure can be interpreted as the papa the cactus as the mama and the amorphous mass as a child a family fractured and vulnerable in the face of an unknown threat though personally I see it slightly differently I see the ominous dark Mass emerging from the right to be the threat itself whilst the landscape is creeping in on to be a plateau of the mind and the difference scattered objects to be a series of different emotions such as hopelessness loneliness vulnerability or the feeling of being trapped which could be emphasized by the cactus that appears to be tied down ultimately this painting transcends a singular interpretation its power lies in its ability to evoke emotions and narratives the desolate landscape serves as a canvas for our own an anxieties and fears inviting us to confront the fragility of existence and the potential for pain within even the most basic relationships I should also point out by the way that this analysis is just one possible interpretation of the painting The Beauty of art like this lies in its subjectivity and each viewer may find their own unique meaning within its enigmatic depths and that's actually something I'd love to hear from you if you have another interpretation or notice something I may have missed so please let me know in the comments below this next work called Noya iner painted in 1929 stands as another prime example of Toni's early surrealist style while the title again offers little to no explanation the painting itself with the minimal and dark imagery it contains radiates a really strong Aura of mystery Intrigue that's very much worth exploring the canvas is dominated by Inky Blackness creating a sense of vastness against this void four biomorphic forms float Defying Gravity identification are they organic growths techn logical relics or products of a subconscious the ambiguity fuels the imagination and as for the cental motif a wispy pale structure occupies the space reminiscent of a ghost or strands smoke light seems to emanate from forms this play of light reinforces the dreamlike quality and creates a sense of depth within the flat canvas a common interpretation you may come across for this piece surrounds Toni's frequent goal to tap the unconscious mind and create dreamlike imagery Noya indaver embodies this perfectly offering a thoughts and desires unburdened by Logic Reason notably KL young a leading purchased the painting in 1929 during a time when Eve tongi was practically unknown to the art world he personally saw it as reflecting human Detachment bleakness potentially influenced by the anxieties of the inter War period young kept it in his study where it influenced and maybe even helped Inspire his theory of a collective 1958 of course tongi himself ultimately left his Works open to interpretation stating that he aimed to voke emotions rather than convey specific messages the viewer is lured in to project their own experiences and feelings onto the canvas finding personal meaning within the ambiguity in terms of technique tongi meticulously rendered the forms with heightening the contrast with their nature this painting stands out as more focused on biomorphic forms and though as we see shortly his later works elements Noya IND deference serves as a powerful and enigmatic work capturing the essence of his creativity and even his most primitive years it haunting connection to the subconscious mind continues to invoke and Inspire it's a real Testament to Toni's ability to translate the dream world into a 1942 plunges us into a realm where recognizable objects morph into strange forms and the familiar landscape devolves into the unknown here tongi paint means not only to depict reality to again evoke our emotions and ignite the viewer's imagination without without any real planning or forethought as he explained himself quote the painting develops before my eyes unfolding its surprises as it quote the composition unfolds like a desolate Beach at Twilight Sandy expanses stretch towards a hazy Horizon immersed in a skylight background while strange biomorphic shapes dominate the resemble petrified bones or eroded Shadows these ambiguous objects defy between the organic and the mechanical artificial the scene is is bathed in an unsettling light a warm glow emanates from our right highlighting the textures Contours of the forms yet this light creates dark contrasts emphasizing the shadows and contributing to the atmosphere is it Dawn breaking or dusk settling the ambiguity adds to the sense of mystery and fluidity of time tongi weaves familiar objects into the seen adding a layer of playful in congruity such as propeller blades bowls of water scattered across the landscape a rusty clamp that sits precariously structure these everyday items stripped of their original contexts become their own characters in this Dreamscape their presence invites viewers to create their own narratives and to decipher hidden meanings within the painting the title indefinite divisibility hints at The painting's Core theme the scene seems endlessly divisible each detail capable of further interpretation and each object could either be attached or infused in some way or simply as one with each other eliminating a sense of Duality the organic forms appear porous suggesting they could fragment further are fluid and meaning is multi-layered according to a wonderfully indepth analysis of his piece on interpretations we can take into account for example Lucien Freud when viewing his painting noted the heightened anxiety created by his use of depaso meaning the state of disorientation experienced in dreams was a form of Illusions as for tongi it was a source of power it's key to remember that many of the most successful surrealists celebrated Madness as both an Liberation Andre Breton said once that in dreams you could kill fly faster love to your heart's content interestingly in 1950 the psychological Institute of Vienna displayed Toni's paintings beside those of schiz frenic patients to see if a public could distinguish between the two as it turns out they could not and this result was one that delighted the surrealists Breton believed that one day Toni's images quote will be made clear with a language that is not yet understood but which people are soon going to read which they are going to talk and which they are going to perceive is best adapted to the new just a painting is an invitation to explore the impossible and the Realms of light Shadow and ambiguous forms to create an unsettling yet captivating atmosphere as surreal art very well should do this work continues to challenge viewers to question their perceptions and delve into the depths of now let's take a look at what could fairly be considered as one of Eve Toni's most famous works in his 1943 painting titled through Birds through glass the painting features strange organic shapes reminiscent of Bones rocks and melted wax these forms defy categorization once again and create a sense of unease and wonder the fiery Reds and oranges beautifully clash with the icy blues and Grays creating a tension that reflects the duality of the title although again the source of light is unclear the contrasting light and shadow it creates add unsettling depth mystery to the scene stones and wheel spokes defy gravity floating in the air like impossible Dreams a tower-like formation composed of balloon shapes giving off the impression of an enigmatic Monument made of molten metal poured into ice cold water the lack of human figures emphasizes the isolation vastness of a landscape and of course the title hints at multiple suggests that freedom and transformation require facing danger but fragility poses a limit maybe it implies that inspiration interpreted as fire and communication interpreted as birds can glass but require considerable effort the title could be Toni's personal reflection on overcoming challenges in his efforts to explore the subconscious Andre Breton stated that tongi quote condensed a few pure elements of matter meeting together and glowing suddenly like particles of dust dancing in a quote when keeping what Breton said into consideration when viewing this piece it truly heightens the concept of how the individual self and the external world are in a constant state of through glass is considered a masterpiece in its own right his captivating imagery and title challenges our perception of reality showing bluntly how the inner and outer worlds are constantly at odds with each other reminding us that there is certainly a physical world outside our minds but how it truly definitively appears can never really be determined only the mind of Eve Toni's Rose of the Four Winds painted in 1950 is a complex and evocative work that embodies the characteristics of his latest style while offering a Fantastical landscape it departs from the Vivid colors and dreamlike softness of his earlier Works presenting a more unsettling and fragmented scene and consisting of a palette the dominant feature is a towering structure on the left reminiscent of a Gothic Cathedral yet composed of a halfhazard assemblage of spiky objects bones and mineral formations like a futuristic place of worship this unsettling Fusion of organic and inorganic materials creates a sense of instability as if despite its dominating presence over a surrounding chaos below it's still delicate able to moment the ground is littered with Jagged debris resembling the rubble of a destroyed City the Steely gray and pink sky adds to the apocalyptic atmosphere evoking feelings of alienation and contrasts with the title Rose hinting a potential Beauty Beyond the immediate despair the scene is bathed in an ominous Cold Light and accentuates for textures this harsh illumination is heightened and emphasizes the stark contrast between the Towering structure landscape Shadow seems to play a pivotal role creating pockets of mystery and hiding potential Secrets within the several interpretations of row of Four Winds exist out there considering that this was painted shortly after World War II the work might reflect the artist's destruction The Bleak landcape and fractured Tower could symbolize the devastation left behind by the conflict the JX position of the imposing Tower and the chaotic landscape may represent the struggle between order and Freedom the title of rose of the Four Winds could symbolize a force of nature lifegiving finally I'd like us to take a look at Toni's very last painting completed just months before his death titled multiplication of the arcs 1954 this work is not only beautiful but a complex tapestry woven with undertones to fully appreciate it let's depths dominated by a vast foreground a looming stormy sky the painting isolation curiously instead of Toni's usual towering structures that were prevalent in a lot of his most famous works here we see fragmented biomorphic shapes resembling bones Pebbles and organic remains scattered across the ground with no dominating structure in symbols of authority the absence of such a structure suggests Decay fragility and mortality considering the timing of a foreshadowing of what awaited the artist earthy Browns yellows and Grays create a melancolic atmosphere while subtle shades of blue offer a glimmer of desires and fears in surrealism here they hint at a connection to the natural impermanence the title refers to the repeated motifs suggesting an abundance of Poss possibilities even in the landscape the play of light and Shadow creates a sense of mystery and depth inviting a viewer to endlessly explore further in terms of this introspective landscape this could be seen as tongi acknowledging both the finitude of life the potential for Renewal within cycles once again the desolate landscape might reflect concerns about the war to destruction and the fragility of human civilization but despite its melancholic undertones the open landscape and subtle light offer a sense of openness and continuity a sense of an ending to which is also endless nonetheless a horizon hidden from view an exponential Journey potential but to be honest with you I feel almost inappropriate for analyzing art like this at times because I really want to emphasize that point of infinite potential which is truly the heart and soul of Toni's work in reality there really are no right or wrong answers tongi embraced the automatic painting drawing technique letting his hand guide the brush allowing for spontaneous unconscious expression so I could interpret his work till the cows come home but will it get us any closer to a definitive answer absolutely not that's like I mentioned in the first painting there may be some details I missed or instances where I've just been overthinking and your interpretations no matter how different they are to mine all the other theories I've uncovered from my research for these paintings should be considered just as valid just because I or someone far better trained in art than me or even someone who new tongi personally can give an interpretation we shouldn't just take it a work of art should be thoroughly investigated by the individual and interpretations of others should be scrutinized so that one may come to their own understanding it's better to think of this video as just a seed that needs watering a finger pointing the way to someone's own experience of Toni's work rather than just taking them straight there Eve tongi not only unconsciously expressed himself in his art a technique that would be adopted by the likes of Jackson Pollock and Mark Rothco but he also executed his paintings with such striking detail in realism I don't think even Salvador Dar accomplished such a skill in his art in fact it's well documented that darly owes a lot of his style to tongi at one point Dary once told Toni's niece Agnes quote I pinched everything from your uncle Eve which to me is what really makes him stand out in the world of surrealism this his concepts are brimming with imagery yet also strikingly minimal simple yet so vast complexity but where Dar was notably items.title: The Shocking Life & Performance Art of Marina Abramović (Part 3)
items.summary: hello everyone blind dweller here and welcome to the third and final episode of the shocking life and performance art of Marina Abramovich apologies that has taken a while to continue this series for those who don't know I needed to take a break for a while because I had other videos that I wanted to release before the end of 2023 and there's a lot of research that has gone into this series so far and the last thing I wanted to do was burn myself out or end up rushing a documentary but now it's a new year I'm fresh and ready to go and looking forward to returning to taking a deep look at this very unique and controversial artist in the last episode we looked at her first ever performances including the infamous piece titled Rhythm zero that a lot of people regard as a most controversial and well-known performance if you haven't seen that episode yet please make sure you do so by the way in this episode we're going to be taking a look at an interesting shift in her work where her performances began to explore much broader and deeper Concepts some even verging on the spiritual starting with a significant period in her life where she would meet a vital character who would briefly become her lover and artistic soulmate named Frank U lysen or as is more widely known Uli we've got a lot to uncover for this Final Chapter so please make yourself comfortable or I guess since we're looking at Marina Abramovich please make yourself uncomfortable and please don't forget to subscribe and hit the notification Bell to catch up with more videos from me on the weird and wonderful side of the art World welcome to another video everyone this is the final installment of the shocking life 1975 following the buzz and uproar that rippled across the art world with rhythm zero Marina Abramovich was invited to Vienna in Austria to perform pieces that were arguably much darker and much more graphic than anything she had performed before yet strangely there isn't much information on these pieces except for what Marina herself writes about in her biography walk through walls in the book she details a rather Grim performance that she was involved in conducted by named Herman Niche who was predominantly Infamous for creating dark and violent spectacles that often use nude performers and real blood with an axe that replicated Unholy and sacrificial rituals the performance Marina took part in would be no different quote that summer Niche staged a performance in a castle outside Vienna called pritz andorf the piece was to last 24 hours there were 60 participants including me most of the others were men some were naked some were dressed all in white I was placed on a wooden stretcher naked blindfolded and the stretcher was leaned against a concrete wall as gloomy music played Niche poured sheep blood and organs eyes and liver over my belly and between my legs things got stranger from there after this had gone on for 12 hours I took off my blindfold and walked away not that I couldn't take it physically I just didn't want to be part of it anymore I understood it was not my thing it was the enormous amount of animals blood and the fact that we had to drink it and that it all all took place in a chapel in the castle it felt like a kind of black mass or banel it seemed so negative to me but at bottom it just was not my story not conceptually or in any other way end quote following this Marina chose to stay in Vienna where she would meet a Swiss artist named Thomas lips who she had a brief relationship with mixed with the profoundly horrific effect of the Herman Niche performance and the brief fling with Thomas lips Abramovich then became inspired to conceptualize her next performance in Vienna where she would subsequently give the title Thomas lips or the lips of Thomas this performance again would have limited information surrounding it compared to our other work with only a few photographs and video clips of the piece still existing today the most well-known photograph being that of a five-pointed star that Marina would carve onto a stomach Marina would detail the performance in her biography as follows I slowly eat 1 kilo of Honey with a silver spoon I slowly drink one liter of red wine out of a crystal glass I break the glass with my right hand I cut a five-pointed star on my stomach with a razor blade I violently whip myself until I no longer feel any pain I lie down on a cross made of ice blocks the heat of a suspended heater pointed at my stomach causes the cut star to bleed and the rest of my body freeze I remain on the ice cross for 30 minutes until the public interrupts the piece by removing the ice blocks from underneath me duration 2 hours end quote although the spectators according to ramovic were familiar with provoc Ive art and performances this particular piece proved to even be too much for them after some Spectators rushed to the stage to cover Marina in coats and help her off the ice she then had to be taken to the hospital not for her wounds from the Whip or the self-inflicted Stars she cut onto her stomach but for her right hand that she had unintentionally gouged when she broke the wine glass that would need a great deal of stitches towards the end of night 1975 on Marina's 29th birthday she received an invitation to take part in a new upcoming performance this time in a gallery in Amsterdam known as the Apple for the Dutch TV show called build spruck in early December Abramovich arrived in Amsterdam to meet the Creator at the airport who was accompanied by another individual a German artist who went by the name of Uli who was to be Marina's guide and assistant for a at that moment Marina seemed to be instantly enthralled by him quote Uli his real name I found out was Frank U lysen but he never used it was in his early 30s tall and skinny with long flowing hair that he tied up in the back with a pair of Chopsticks a fact that was immediately interesting to me because I did my hair the exact same way the other interesting thing was was that the two halves of his face were different the left side was shaved smooth and powdered with a plucked eyebrow and light Rouge on his lips the right side was stubbly and a little greasy with a normal eyebrow and no makeup if you saw either side in profile you would get a completely different impression masculine on one side feminine on the other end quote as she spent time with him in Amsterdam they would discover quite surprising similarities to each other the biggest coincidence being that they shared the same birthday of November 30th as time went on they spent more time with each other and began to form relationship but this ultimately would only be the beginning of a partnership that would change both of their lives falling deeply in love with Uli a man who she truly felt was destined for her made leaving Amsterdam to once again return to Belgrade all the more difficult not to mention that she was still married to Nesha palovich and living with her mother it was a desire and one that would have to be kept secret for a long time on top of this she was also forced to resign from her teaching job due to the emerging pictures of her Rhythm performances that would cause a scandal at this stage Abramovich was left with little choice to plan her escape from Belgrade for good and to live with Uli she packed light only taking a handful of belongings with the majority of her things only being a portfolio of her work and she secretly left on a
